_comment: Tunable numeric parameters for make_pinyin_font.py. All values are stated at the 1000-UPM reference grid; the build script must scale them linearly when the source font's UPM differs (e.g. baseline_at_upm_1000 * actual_upm / 1000). See Output_font_requirements.md.

ruby_geometry_at_upm_1000._comment_baseline_y: Y-coordinate of the ruby baseline (where non-descender letters sit). FZ-extracted ruby and Latin-composed ruby both align on this baseline; descenders (g/p/q/y) hang ~64 units below. Raise to widen the gap above the base CJK glyph (typical CJK yMax ≈ 840), lower to tighten it. Current gap: ~124 (non-descender) / ~60 (descender). Ascent values above are sized to baseline_y + em + headroom_above_ruby.
ruby_geometry_at_upm_1000._comment_max_overflow_factor: Maximum width of a composed ruby relative to the CJK advance (1.0 = ruby never exceeds the cell, 1.15 = up to 15% overflow allowed). Long syllables (zhuāng, chuáng, shuāng, …) hit this cap and are uniformly scaled down to fit, so values >1.0 cause adjacent ruby pinyins to overlap. Keep at 1.0 unless you accept neighbor overlap.
